obligations.statement: One request is evaluated against one exact semantic epoch.
Inbound request fields are limited to authorization_request_id, authentication_evidence_ref, route_id, and session_ref.
Exactly one authentication-evidence record resolves for the supplied evidence reference.
Authentication evidence is trusted and not revoked.
Authentication evidence is current and unexpired at the single decision time.
Exactly one route binding resolves for the supplied route identifier.
The resolved route binding is enabled and complete.
The evidence revision is captured from trusted state.
The route revision is captured from trusted state.
The evidence and resolved session identify the same session.
The evidence and resolved session identify the same subject.
The trusted authorization command copies permission from the route binding exactly.
The trusted authorization command copies the scope-evidence reference from the route binding exactly.
The authorization-state snapshot joins the current authorization revision.
All active-role rows join the captured active-role revision.
All grant rows join the captured grant revision.
Exactly one trusted scope-evidence row matches the exact route scope.
An exact active-role grant supplies the exact route permission.
Trusted-input and authorization-state reads occur inside one transaction.
All time predicates use one decision time.
Provider, transaction, query, and commit uncertainty fails closed.
The externally observable decision is exactly ALLOW or DENY.
Every obligation is justified by a typed derivation; token or name presence is not proof.
Evidence follows one ordered lineage; unordered set membership is not proof.
An Auth-specific theorem and exact Rust projection prove the selected meta-type correspondence.

closure_rule: The denominator is closed only when all 25 unique obligation identifiers are present exactly once and the 24 plus 1 partition sums are exact.
claim_ceiling: This is an exact prototype denominator, not evidence that any obligation has passed.
